summary: Ephemeral IO-heavy tenant triggered dedicated pool slot oscillation and sustained p99 throughput jitter
description:
Issue summary: Customer (MapleAI) observed recurring p95/p99 throughput jitter and transient request timeouts from their dedicated pool between 2026-02-24 23:40 UTC and 2026-02-25 02:10 UTC. The pattern looks like repeated slot reclamation and rapid autoscaler activity tied to a short-lived tenant that produced high NVLink and PCIe I/O, not purely GPU compute.

Impact: Affected customer's production endpoints (~10 routes) experienced p99 latency spikes from ~180ms to 2.8s and a measurable drop in tokens/sec throughput (~28% at peak). No model-level errors; errors manifested as 502/504 and occasional kernel queue timeouts. Customer reported user-facing failures for ~80% of requests during the 30-minute worst window.

Observed behavior: Dedicated pool showed oscillating allocation counts (slot add/remove churn), autoscaler logs show rapid scale-up then immediate shrink with many short-lived GPUs entering the pool. Host-level telemetry recorded high NVLink utilization and PCIe retransmits on a subset of hosts hosting the noisy tenant. Prefix cache metrics remained stable.

Hypothesis: A tenant issued a mix of many short, high-concurrency streams with heavy tensor copy / I/O patterns (large prompt attachments and streaming checkpoint writes) that caused host-level IO saturation and caused our scheduler to evict or reassign slots rapidly. Autoscaler interprets the temporary increase in queue length as demand and spins up more capacity, which then collapses as eviction/IO fails, causing oscillation.

Timeline: 2026-02-24 23:36 UTC - first p50/p95 drift noted in customer telemetry. 23:40 UTC - cluster autoscaler triggered +6 GPUs for pool. 23:46 UTC - NVLink errors spike on hosts 3/7/11. 23:48 UTC - scheduler reports 12 slot preemptions in 8 minutes. 00:10 UTC - customer reports 502s. 01:05 UTC - autoscaler attempted a second scale-up; short lived. 02:15 UTC - transient return to baseline after noisy tenant ramp-down.

Attachments: collection of p99 graphs, autoscaler event log, sample gc/daemon logs will be added to ticket attachments section.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route heavy mix of short-request streams (>200 concurrent short streams/sec) to a dedicated pool route pinned to small-batch service profile.
2) Include large client-side request bodies that require host-side staging (e.g., long attachment or embedded context >1MB).
3) Observe host NVLink/PCIe counters and scheduler autoscaler events within 5-30 minutes of sustained burst.
4) Verify that CPU and GPU compute utilization remain moderate while host I/O metrics saturate.
metrics: Host NVLink errors: spike from 0 to 30/min on affected hosts
investigation_notes: 2026-02-25 04:20 UTC - SRE Diego Martinez: Captured kernel traces from affected hosts; kernel queue shows increased retry attempts while compute kernels remained queued but waiting for DMA completion.
2026-02-25 06:05 UTC - Infra Eng (Maya Li): Verified short-lived tenant 'tenant-876' produced 18k small streams over 22 minutes; per-tenant IO bytes were 2.1GB/min, top 3 hosts skewed.

2026-02-25 08:12 UTC - Runtime Eng (Omar Khalid): Confirmed autoscaler reacted to queue-growth metric which is tainted by transient IO-backed queues; suggested tuning cooldown and min-stable-window for the dedicated pool type.
2026-02-25 09:35 UTC - Support (Aisha): Coordinated with MapleAI to throttle client-side concurrency as temporary mitigation and collected request samples for root-cause reproduction.
Note: We intentionally did not roll back any kernel changes and preserved logs for postmortem.
resolution:
Workaround applied: In coordination with MapleAI we temporarily limited route concurrency to 60 streams per second and increased autoscaler stable-window to 90s for the dedicated pool. This stopped the rapid add/remove oscillation and restored p99 near baseline.

Next actions: 1) Engineering to add an I/O-saturation detector to the scheduler to avoid treating IO-backed queue growth as compute demand (ticket created: infra-io-detector). 2) Consider adding per-tenant IO quotas for dedicated pools. 3) Run targeted repro with infra+runtime to validate fixes.

Status: Mitigated; awaiting permanent change from infra team. No code rollout yet.
